title: Symbolum Theodori Mopsuesteni Et Ejus Refutatio
author: Marius Mercator
source: Translated by Claude from tmp777.tmp777.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: ut de haeresi Pelagiana, seu Coelestiana, quamb de- fendendam et sequendam suscepit, ab ipso confir- maretur; atque inde, velut instructior, octo contra fidem catholicam potius quam contra sanctae memo- riae Augustinum volumina illa, ut putat, prudentis- sima conderet.
passages.english: so that he might be confirmed by him concerning the Pelagian, or Caelestian, heresy which he had undertaken to defend and follow; and that from there, as if better equipped, he might compose those eight volumes, most learned as he thinks, against the catholic faith rather than against Augustine of holy memory.
passages.notes: The sentence continues from the preceding context: 'he' is Julian of Eclanum and 'him' is Theodore [of Mopsuestia]. 'quamb' read as 'quam' (stray footnote mark); hyphenated line-breaks joined. 'prudentissima' is rendered 'most learned' (literally 'most wise/prudent'); the phrase 'ut putat' ('as he thinks') is ironic.
